# The code that is generated by Visual Studio

```
private void FormLoad(object sender, EventArgs e)
{
// TODO: This line of code loads data into the
// 'mMBooksDataSet.Products'.
// You can move, or remove it, as needed.
this.productsTableAdapter.Fill(this.mMBooksDataSet);
}
```

```
private void voidProductsBindingNavigatorSaveItem_Click(object sender, EventArgs e)
{
this.Validate();
this.productsBindingSource.EndEdit();
this.tableAdapterManager.UpdateAll(this.mMBooksDataSet);
}
```

# The syntax of the Fill method

```
tableAdapter.Fill(dataSet.TableName)
```

# The syntax of the UpdateAll method

```
tableAdapterManager.UpdateAll(dataSet)
```

# Description

+   - Visual Studio automatically generates the code when you drag a data source onto a form. If necessary, you can edit this code.
- The generated code uses the Fill method of the TableAdapter object that's generated for to read data from the database, and it uses the UpdateAll method of the TableAdapterManager object that's generated for the dataset to write data to the database. It uses the EndEdit method of the BindingSource to save any changes that have been made to the current row to the dataset.
- The Validate method causes the Validating and Validated events of the control that is losing the focus to be fired. You can use the Validating event to perform any required data validation for the form.
- Users of a DataGridView control can sort the rows by clicking on a column header and dragging the column separators to the left or right. They can also reorder the columns by dragging them if option is enabled (see figure 19-9).
